evidence: Verg. A. 9.24: multa deōs ōrāns (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically to beg, beseech, the gods among others; used absolutely, “to pray”, in the Vulgate and the Church (Lewis & Short). Ōrēmus, let us pray; ōrāre prō aliquō, to pray for someone.

evidence: Cic. ND 1.119: deōs colere, precārī, venerārīque (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Cicero’s verb for praying to the gods; the school dialogues use it for saying one’s prayers (precātus es Deum?, Corderius).

phrases.english: Let’s pray first (before the meal, or before getting up from it).

phrases.latin: An precātus es Deum? — Cum prīmum frāter mē pexuit, precātus sum.
phrases.english: Have you said your prayers? — As soon as my brother had combed my hair, I said them.

sources: Lewis & Short: oro · Lewis & Short: precor
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. pray (religious).
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-vulgata, loci-schottenius, loci-corderius), checked against the editions named there.
